name: Action Physics Verification
description: Validates physical plausibility of human actions — AI video often violates Newton's laws in body movement dynamics.
mechanism:
This method verifies whether human actions depicted in video obey Newtonian mechanics and biomechanical constraints:

1. **Pose Estimation and Trajectory Extraction**: The method extracts 2D or 3D body joint positions per frame using a pose estimator (e.g., OpenPose or MediaPipe). Joint trajectories are smoothed using a Savitzky-Golay filter (window = 5 frames, order = 3) and differentiated to obtain velocities and accelerations. For each body segment (forearm, thigh, torso, etc.), the method computes the center of mass trajectory and angular velocity. AI-generated videos frequently produce joint trajectories with discontinuities — sudden teleportation of limbs between frames — or unrealistic acceleration magnitudes that violate the biomechanical limits of human muscles.

2. **Center-of-Mass Dynamics Verification**: Newton's second law requires that the center of mass (CoM) of the human body follows a parabolic trajectory during aerial phases (no ground contact) and stays within the base of support during stance phases. The method estimates the body's CoM from segmental masses (Winter, 2009) and verifies: (a) during jumps or airborne actions, CoM follows a parabolic arc with downward acceleration ≈ 9.81 m/s², (b) during standing actions, CoM projection remains within the support polygon formed by the feet, (c) during walking, CoM follows the inverted pendulum model. Violations indicate physically implausible motion typical of AI generation.

3. **Joint Torque Feasibility**: From joint angles and accelerations, the method estimates the net joint torques required to produce the observed motion using inverse dynamics. These computed torques are compared against known maximum voluntary torques for human joints (e.g., knee extension: ~200 Nm, elbow flexion: ~80 Nm). Actions requiring torques exceeding physiological limits by more than 2× are flagged as physically implausible. AI-generated videos often show movements that would require superhuman joint torques — for instance, rapid arm movements with no corresponding body counter-rotation.

4. **Action-Reaction Consistency**: Newton's third law requires that every action has an equal and opposite reaction. During ground contact, the ground reaction force must equal the rate of change of total body momentum. The method verifies this by checking that: (a) jumping height is consistent with the impulse during push-off, (b) landing deceleration is consistent with impact dynamics, (c) throwing motions show appropriate recoil in the torso. AI generators often violate action-reaction by producing movements where the character appears to float, defy inertia, or execute actions without appropriate momentum transfer.
parameters:
Pose estimator: OpenPose / MediaPipe
Body segments: 15 (standard biomechanical model)
Segmental mass model: Winter (2009)
Savitzky-Golay filter: window 5, order 3
Gravitational acceleration: 9.81 m/s²
Torque feasibility threshold: 2× maximum voluntary torque
CoM parabolic fit R² threshold: > 0.95
Minimum video length: 30 frames
Frame rate: ≥ 24 fps required
accuracy: 74–83% accuracy for detecting physically implausible actions in AI-generated videos. CoM dynamics verification achieves F1-score of 0.79 for detecting aerial phase violations. Joint torque feasibility analysis most effective for detecting fast actions (precision = 0.85). Performance depends heavily on pose estimation quality and camera angle.
source: Winter, D. A. (2009). Biomechanics and Motor Control of Human Movement. 4th Edition, Wiley.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated videos with physically implausible human actions. Verifying authenticity of sports and action footage. Forensic analysis of surveillance video for deepfake detection. Quality assessment of motion capture and animation systems.
strengths:
• Physics-based constraints provide objective, content-independent verification criteria
• Center-of-mass analysis is robust to partial occlusion
• Joint torque feasibility catches subtle violations invisible to human observers
• Action-reaction verification detects floating/sliding artifacts common in AI video
• Complementary to appearance-based deepfake detection methods
limitations:
• Requires reliable pose estimation — errors in joint positions propagate to physics calculations
• Monocular depth ambiguity limits 3D torque estimation accuracy
• Unusual but physically valid actions (gymnastics, martial arts) may trigger false positives
• Slow movements produce small accelerations that are difficult to verify against noise
• Camera motion and lens distortion affect apparent trajectories
